aboutPage.metaDescription: SPORE is built by Benoît Baqué de Sariac, an engineer in Nantes. Solo developer, transparent side project, micro-entreprise SoBaq. The thinking behind a research collision engine for interdisciplinary hypotheses.
aboutPage.title: About SPORE
aboutPage.section1_p1_after: from Nantes. Solo developer, engineer by training, polymath by temperament. A structured side project, hosted and maintained autonomously.
aboutPage.section1_p1_before: SPORE is designed, built, and operated by
aboutPage.section1_p2: No team, no fundraising, no institutional badge. One person who codes, reads, tunes the prompts, pays the server, and watches the hypotheses come out. This transparency is constitutive of the project: SPORE claims scientific rigour, and rigour begins with naming who speaks.
aboutPage.section1_p3: If you wish to discuss the project, send a comment, flag an error, or imagine a collaboration: an email is enough.
aboutPage.section2_p1: The most disruptive scientific advances often arise at the intersection of distant domains. Penicillin (microbiology × mould chemistry), CRISPR (bacterial immunology × genome editing), PageRank (academic citations × linear algebra), AlphaFold (bioinformatics × deep learning) — each one a case where the meeting of distant disciplines yielded an advance no isolated field would have formulated.
aboutPage.section2_p2_before: SPORE rests on a wager: to automate the
aboutPage.section2_p2_after: of these unexplored intersections. Not to replace scientific work — an LLM does not run experiments and validates nothing against the real — but to generate, continuously, the plausible bridges no one has had the time or reflex to formulate. A structured serendipity engine.
aboutPage.section3_step1: Draws two scientific domains at random from a corpus of 500 (sourced from OpenAlex)
aboutPage.section3_step2: Generates, via LLM (DeepSeek + Claude), a hypothetical causal bridge between the two
aboutPage.section3_step3: Submits this bridge to a critique pipeline: devil's advocate, methodologist, domain expert, panel of 5 AI reviewers
aboutPage.section3_step4: Verifies every bibliographic reference through the Semantic Scholar API (zero hallucination tolerated)
aboutPage.section3_step5: Publishes the result as a structured brief: formal hypothesis, three-phase experimental protocol with quantified GO/NO-GO criteria, falsifiable predictions, clickable evidence base
aboutPage.section3_outro_before: Across 2,095 collisions explored, 38 briefs published. The 98.2% kill rate is public and assumed. The mean cost per brief is $0.51, for a cumulative total of $19.49 — figures available in real time on the
aboutPage.section4_b1_after: in the classical sense. SPORE produces hypotheses, not results. Hypotheses must be confronted with reality by human researchers.
aboutPage.section4_b2_strong: Not a public-facing science media outlet
aboutPage.section4_b2_after: . The French vulgarisation layer aids diffusion, but the product addresses primarily researchers, R&D engineers, working polymaths, and PhD students.
aboutPage.section4_b3_after: . Each brief carries a badge: « AI-generated hypothesis · Pre-publication · To be tested experimentally ». This is the epistemically correct stance.
aboutPage.section4_b4_strong: Not a funded or affiliated project
aboutPage.section4_b4_after: . No badge, no oversight, no hidden agenda. Just a curious developer who believes analogical thinking can be tooled.
aboutPage.section5_p1: SPORE crosses texts about science, not science itself. The scientific literature is a filtered, delayed, and socially constructed representation of reality. SPORE can identify gaps in the scientific discourse, not in nature. The bridges it produces are plausible in a linguistic sense — not necessarily productive in an experimental one. This distinction is central, and SPORE owns it.
aboutPage.section5_p2: The five AI reviewers do not constitute independent validation: they are projections of the same representational space as the generator. They detect internal inconsistencies, not contradiction by reality. The only validation that matters is experimental, and it lies beyond SPORE's perimeter.
aboutPage.section6_intro: SPORE is free during the launch phase. In the longer term:
aboutPage.section6_b1_after: — pay-per-use, unlimited access to the purchased brief.
aboutPage.section6_b2_after: — 5 briefs/month on domains of your choice (in preparation, planned for June 2026).
aboutPage.section6_b3_after: — propose two domains, SPORE generates an unprecedented hypothesis with protocol and bibliography in 24 hours. First collision offered during launch.
aboutPage.section6_b4_middle: — a free PDF of the eight strongest hypotheses from the first six months, sent by email
aboutPage.section6_outro_before: For research teams or corporate R&D groups interested in custom integration: an email to
aboutPage.section6_outro_after: is enough to start the conversation.
aboutPage.section7_quote: A well-documented dead end is worth more than a glib unification.
aboutPage.section7_p1: This is the line that guides SPORE. Success is not measured by the number of briefs published, but by the quality of the hypotheses generated and the honesty of their status. Each brief is an exploratory proposition, delivered with its doubts intact.

methodologyPage.metaDescription: How SPORE computes (or does not) its metrics: novelty score, panel consensus, kill rate, reference verification. Transparency about the methods and their acknowledged limits.
methodologyPage.title: SPORE methodology
methodologyPage.intro: This page documents, transparently, how the metrics displayed on SPORE actually work. The project claims scientific rigour — rigour begins with stating honestly how each figure is produced, including when the method is imperfect.
methodologyPage.novelty_what_text: an estimate, by the LLM itself, of how original the formulated hypothesis is relative to the recent scientific literature found through Semantic Scholar.
methodologyPage.novelty_how_textBefore: after querying the Semantic Scholar API on the hypothesis's keywords, SPORE submits the full set of papers returned to the LLM (DeepSeek or Claude depending on the stage) with an explicit instruction:
methodologyPage.novelty_how_quote: « assess how novel this hypothesis is against what already exists »
methodologyPage.novelty_how_textAfter: . The LLM returns a score between 0 and 1 and a categorical verdict
methodologyPage.novelty_not_text: an objective measure based on embeddings, cosine distance, or statistical analysis of the citation graph. There is no mathematical formula behind it. This is a heuristic self-assessment.
methodologyPage.novelty_limit1: The score reflects the LLM's self-evaluation bias (a tendency to overrate its own outputs, or to underrate them when trained for caution).
methodologyPage.novelty_limit2: The temporal window of comparison depends on the Semantic Scholar results and is not strictly bounded.
methodologyPage.novelty_limit3: A « rediscovered » concept that has existed for 30 years but does not appear in the Semantic Scholar top 10 may be scored as novel.
methodologyPage.novelty_limit4: The mean score observed across published briefs is 0.80 — this is a signal of systematic over-evaluation, not a neutral measurement.
methodologyPage.novelty_read_textBefore: use the novelty score as a
methodologyPage.novelty_read_textAfter: indicator (this hypothesis seems more novel than that one, according to the model), not as an absolute measure. To assess the genuine novelty of a hypothesis, read the « Novelty assessment » section of the brief, which lists the closest existing works identified.
methodologyPage.novelty_planned_textBefore: a future sprint (referenced in the backlog as
methodologyPage.novelty_planned_textAfter: ) will implement an algorithmic score based on semantic distance (sentence-transformers embeddings) and the absence of co-occurrence in the corpus. The current score will be retained alongside it for comparison.
methodologyPage.panel_what_text: the weighted average of the individual scores given by the five AI reviewers of the post-publication panel.
methodologyPage.panel_how_textBefore: each reviewer (Methodologist, Domain expert, Devil's advocate, Industrial reviewer, Funding strategist) attaches a score out of 10 according to its own criteria, accompanied by a categorical verdict
methodologyPage.panel_how_textAfter: and a confidence rating (0 to 1). The
methodologyPage.panel_how_textEnd: is a weighted mean by each reviewer's confidence.
methodologyPage.panel_not_text: an independent validation. The five reviewers are projections of the same linguistic representational space as the one that generated the hypothesis. They detect internal inconsistencies, not experimental contradiction.
methodologyPage.killRate_what_text: the proportion of attempted collisions that do not yield a published brief.
methodologyPage.killRate_how_textBefore: a public counter, updated on each cycle, visible on the
methodologyPage.killRate_why_text: across 2,095 collisions attempted, 38 briefs published (a 98.2% kill rate). This figure is NOT a defect — it is rigorous selection at work. The majority of random domain pairs do not yield a scientifically defensible causal bridge. Publishing every collision would amount to publishing 95% noise.
methodologyPage.refs_what_text: every DOI cited in a published brief has been technically verified through the Semantic Scholar API.
methodologyPage.refs_means_text: the DOI exists, it points to an article identified on Semantic Scholar, and the title and authors retrieved match what is cited in the brief.
methodologyPage.refs_notMeans_text: the conclusion cited has NOT been verified. SPORE guarantees that the references exist and are correctly identified. SPORE does not guarantee that the LLM has correctly interpreted the content of each article. For critical briefs, always verify the conclusion by consulting the original article.
methodologyPage.costs_textBefore: All LLM inference costs are published in real time on the
methodologyPage.costs_textEnd: . Cumulative cost since launch: visible publicly.

howItWorks.metaDescription: From domain collision to research brief: the SPORE pipeline step by step, with 5 AI reviewers, Semantic Scholar grounding, and zero bibliographic hallucination.
howItWorks.title: From collision to brief
howItWorks.subtitle: Eleven steps. Two pipelines: L0 generates the hypotheses; the post-🔥 stage validates the strongest ones in depth.
howItWorks.funnelTitle: The funnel in numbers (100 typical collisions)
howItWorks.principle1_desc: The system generates and validates; it does not replace human judgement. Every brief is an invitation to think, not a conclusion.
howItWorks.principle2_desc: Every reference is verified through Semantic Scholar. If a DOI does not resolve, it is dropped. Citations are the foundation.
howItWorks.principle3_desc: Methodologist, domain expert, devil's advocate, industrial reviewer, funding strategist. No blind spot. Every doubt is voiced.
